prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1224; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a rear-end collision at a slow-moving intersection and a knee injury from the impact. The claim was opened and the vehicle was flagged for an inspection.

Entry 2: The driver is listed on the policy and was the operator of the insured vehicle at the time of loss. Coverage was in force when the incident occurred, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Police report and two independent witnesses place the claimant inside the vehicle at the scene and confirm the sequence of events as described. The other driver's statement matches the claimant's account.

Entry 4: Photos from the scene and the repair estimate show damage concentrated at the rear of the vehicle, which is largely consistent with the reported impact. No prior damage to the vehicle appears in our records or the inspection notes.

Entry 5: Claimant gave the same account of the collision in each call and written statement, with no changes to the sequence or location. Knee complaints were reviewed against the force of the crash and appear consistent with that kind of impact.

Entry 6: Medical records show no earlier injury to the same knee and no prior treatment on file for that body area. Treatment followed a typical course, with physical therapy tapering as the claimant's mobility improved.

Entry 7: Adjuster recommends settlement review based on the documented treatment course and the consistent evidence across the police report, photos, witness statements, and vehicle inspection.
